topic.label: Management Science and Engineering
topic.desc: Management Science and Engineering: quantitative methods for decisions, operations, finance, organisations and technology strategy.

concepts: Formulating and solving linear, integer, network and convex programs that allocate scarce resources under constraints.
Probability models of uncertain systems, including Markov chains, queues and discrete-event simulation.
Structuring choices under uncertainty with decision trees, utility, value of information and risk preferences.
Design and control of production, inventory, logistics and service operations.
Valuation, portfolio construction and risk measurement for investments, projects and derivatives.
How firms organise people, adopt technology, innovate and compete, studied with organisation theory and strategy frameworks.
skills: Turns a business problem into decision variables, objective and constraints, solves it and checks feasibility and dual prices.
Builds mixed-integer models for scheduling and assignment and verifies the returned schedule satisfies every constraint.
Reports reduced costs, shadow prices and allowable ranges and checks them by re-solving with perturbed parameters.
Computes waiting times and utilisation for M/M/c and related queues and checks closed-form results against simulation.
Builds transition matrices, solves steady-state and absorption probabilities and checks rows sum to one and results converge.
Simulates process flows with random arrivals and reports confidence intervals checked by replication count and variance.
Builds and rolls back decision trees to expected value or utility and checks probabilities and payoffs are coherent.
Computes expected value of perfect and sample information and checks it never exceeds the value of perfect information.
Elicits utility curves and risk tolerance from stakeholders and checks answers for consistency across lotteries.
Sets EOQ, reorder point and safety stock for items and checks fill rates by simulation against the target service level.
Fits time-series forecasts to demand history and checks accuracy with holdout error metrics.
Chooses facility locations and flows to minimise cost and checks capacity and demand balance in the solution.
Discounts project cash flows to NPV and IRR and checks results under alternative discount rates.
Computes efficient frontiers and optimal weights and checks the covariance matrix is positive semidefinite.
Prices options with binomial and Black-Scholes models and checks the two methods converge and satisfy put-call parity.
Maps structure, incentives and coordination in a team or firm and checks findings against interview or survey evidence.
Fits diffusion curves to adoption data and checks fit quality and forecast plausibility.
Analyses industry structure and competitive positioning and checks claims against market and firm data.
